lines.japanese: 「さて、そろそろ勉強──」
lines.english: “Well, time to study—”

lines.japanese: 一息ついて背もたれに体重をかけたとき、視界の隅でパパッと原色の光が瞬いた。
lines.english: I had just settled back and put my weight against the chair when primary-colored light flickered at the edge of my vision.

lines.japanese: ランプの点滅に一瞬遅れて、机の上の子機から着信音が鳴りだした。
lines.english: A moment after the lamp began to blink, the cordless handset on my desk started ringing.

lines.japanese: 僕の携帯電話じゃなくて（当然だ、家族しか番号を知らないんだから）、羽田の家の一般回線だ。誰だろう、叔母さんかな。
lines.english: It was not my cell phone—naturally, since only my family knew the number—but the Haneda household’s landline. Who could it be? My aunt, perhaps.

lines.japanese: 僕は子機を充電器から取りあげて通話ボタンを押した。
lines.english: I lifted the handset from its charger and pressed Talk.

lines.japanese: 「はい。羽田です」
lines.english: “Hello, Haneda residence.”

lines.japanese: 「夜分に失礼いたします。美空学園三年Ａ組の渡来と申しますが、鷹志さんはご在宅でしょうか」
lines.english: “Forgive me for calling so late. This is Asuka Watarai of Class 3-A at Misora Academy. May I speak with Takashi, please?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: その声を電話越しに聞くのは初めてだった。いつもより大人びたよそゆきの口調。突然のことに、僕の頭は真っ白になった。
lines.english: I had never heard her voice over the telephone before. The polite voice she used with strangers made her sound older than usual. The surprise emptied my mind.

lines.japanese: 「え？　あれ？　え、えっ？　あハイ、僕──おれですけど」
lines.english: “What? Wait—what? Oh, yes, this is—I mean, yeah, it’s me.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ほんとに羽田君……？」
lines.english: “Is this really Haneda…?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “Y-yes.”

lines.japanese: 微妙に疑ってる。僕はそんなに変な声を出してたんだろうか。
lines.english: A hint of suspicion. Had my voice sounded so very strange?

lines.japanese: 「そっか……」
lines.english: “Oh…”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いま電話へーき？」
lines.english: “Can you talk right now?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、ああ、ええーっと、そうだな……うん、まあ、あの、大丈夫だけど」
lines.english: “What? Oh, um… let me think. Yes, I suppose. I mean, it’s fine.”

lines.japanese: 暇で暇で仕方なかったくせに、なんとなく忙しぶってしまった。電話の向こうで、くすっと吹きだす息遣いが聞こえた。
lines.english: Though I had been desperately bored, I found myself pretending to be busy. Across the line, I heard a small breath of laughter.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの、緊張してる？」
lines.english: “What’s wrong? Are you nervous?”

lines.japanese: 「まさか」
lines.english: “Of course not.”

lines.japanese: 僕は嘘をついた。
lines.english: I lied.

lines.japanese: 「いき──いきなりだったから、ちょっとバタバタしててさ」
lines.english: “It was just so sud—sudden. I was in the middle of things.”

lines.japanese: 冷静を装ったけれど、噛んでしまったのはちょっと格好悪かった。
lines.english: I tried to play it cool, but stumbling over my words was kind of embarrassing.

lines.japanese: 「そっか。じゃ緊張したの私だけだ。もー、五回ぐらい名簿閉じたり開いたりしちゃったよね」
lines.english: “I see. Then I was the only nervous one. Honestly, I must have opened and closed the class list five times.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、そうなんだ……」
lines.english: “Oh. Really…”

lines.japanese: ほとんど冗談で決めた“Ｗさんと遊びに行く”なんて課題が甦ってなんとなく落ちつかず、僕は電話機を耳にあてながら、意味もなく席を立って部屋の隅へ移った。
lines.english: The half-joking assignment ‘Go somewhere fun with W.’ returned to me and left me strangely restless. Holding the phone to my ear, I rose for no reason and moved to a corner of the room.

lines.japanese: 「あの、それで何の……」
lines.english: “So, um… what did you—”

lines.japanese: 「あれー、気が付いたら置いといたジュース空っぽー」
lines.english: “Oh, look. The juice I left here is all gone.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「あはは。名簿閉じるたび、くぴくぴ飲んでたから」
lines.english: “Ah-ha-ha. I took a sip every time I closed the list.”

lines.japanese: くぴくぴ……想像したらなんだかちょっと可愛かった。
lines.english: Sip after sip… The picture was somehow rather charming.

lines.japanese: 「へえ、渡来さんでも緊張することあるんだ」
lines.english: “I didn’t know even you got nervous, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 僕は自分のひどい緊張を棚にあげた。
lines.english: I conveniently ignored the desperate state of my own nerves.

lines.japanese: 「ね。我ながら意外。わりと根性据わってる方だと思ってたんだけど。うん、よく考えたら私、同い年の男の子に自分から電話するのって初めてだったよね」
lines.english: “Right? Even I’m surprised. I thought I was pretty gutsy, too. But now that I think about it, that was the first time I’d ever been the one to call a boy my age.”

lines.japanese: 「え、それも意外……」
lines.english: “That surprises me too…”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？　私ずっと『羽田君一筋』だったでしょー」
lines.english: “Why? I’ve always been faithful to you and you alone, haven’t I?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そっか、あはは……」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Ha ha…”

lines.japanese: 知らないひとが聞いたら、ものすごく羨ましがられる会話なんだろうな、これ……。
lines.english: Anyone who overheard this conversation would probably be consumed with envy…

lines.japanese: 「で……なに、いきなり」
lines.english: “So… why call out of nowhere?”

lines.japanese: 「いきなりだった？」
lines.english: “Was it out of nowhere?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、そういう意味じゃなくて、だって、最近ずっと話してなかったじゃん」
lines.english: “Oh, no, that’s not what I meant. It’s just, we haven’t talked in a while, you know?”

lines.japanese: 「ほう」
lines.english: “Oh?”

lines.japanese: 電話の向こうで声が止まった。渡来さんはケータイからなんだろう、無線端末特有の遠さが感じられた。
lines.english: Her voice stopped. She must have been calling from a cell phone; the peculiar distance of a wireless connection lay between us.

lines.japanese: 「もしもし？　聞こえてる？」
lines.english: “Hello? Can you hear me?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん。聞こえてる……」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes, I can…”

lines.japanese: 「そう、じゃあ用件は？」
lines.english: “All right. Then what did you need?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ用件、ん、っとね……うん、あの、そう、明日の世界史、何ページまでだったかなあって思って」
lines.english: “Right, what I needed. Um… well… yes. I was wondering what page tomorrow’s world-history exam went up to.”

lines.japanese: 「世界史の範囲ね。分かった、ちょっと待って」
lines.english: “The world-history material. Got it. Just a second.”

lines.japanese: 僕は慌てて子機を左手に持ちかえて、残る手で机の上のノートをめくった。
lines.english: I hurriedly shifted the handset to my left hand and used the other to leaf through the notebooks on my desk.

lines.japanese: そのぐらいのことだったら、クラスにうまく溶けこんでる彼女には、他に聞ける級友がいくらでもいるように思えたけど、それはあえて口にしなかった。
lines.english: If that was all she needed, it seemed to me that someone as thoroughly at home in our class as she was must have any number of classmates she could ask. I kept that thought to myself.

lines.japanese: 「いい？　ええとね、２１４ページの、アメリカ独立革命から──」
lines.english: “Ready? Okay, page 214, starting with the American Revolution—”

lines.japanese: 僕は試験前に板書した内容を、担当教師のワンポイントアドバイスを交えながら電話の向こうへ伝えた。彼女はふんふんと耳のくすぐったくなるような相槌を吹きかけながら聞いていた。
lines.english: I relayed what the teacher had written on the board before the exam, adding the odd pointer he had given us along the way. She listened from the other end of the line, breathing little mm-hmms that seemed to tickle my ear.

lines.japanese: 「──で、だいたいそんな感じ」
lines.english: “—and that’s about it.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。助かった……うん。ありがと……」
lines.english: “Okay. That really helped… Yeah. Thanks…”

lines.japanese: 僕はノートを閉じた。渡来さんの声はいつもより少しだけ湿度が高いように思えた。
lines.english: I closed the notebook. Watarai’s voice seemed to carry a little more moisture than usual.

lines.japanese: 「テスト疲れ？」
lines.english: “Exams wearing you out?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なんで？」
lines.english: “What? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、なんとなく……ごめん、気のせいか」
lines.english: “No reason, you just… Sorry. Guess I imagined it.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、疲れてるよ。ちょっとね。昼間、面白いことがあって。まだ興奮冷めやらぬって感じだよね」
lines.english: “No, I am tired. A little, anyway. Something interesting happened earlier today, and I guess I’m still excited about it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうなんだ、はは……」
lines.english: “Oh, really? Ha ha…”
“Ha…”

lines.japanese: 僕はまた電話機を持ちかえて、汗ばんだてのひらを服で拭った。彼女の言う「面白いこと」が何なのか興味はあったけど、僕はそれについて尋ねてもいいんだろうか。
lines.english: I changed hands again and wiped my clammy palm on my clothes. I wanted to know what this ‘something interesting’ had been, but was I allowed to ask?

lines.japanese: とにかく沈黙はまずい。通話口から「それじゃ」が出てくるより先に会話を繋げなくては。
lines.english: Whatever I did, I could not let the silence settle. I had to keep the conversation alive before an “Anyway, I should go” came drifting through the receiver.

lines.japanese: どうしよう。面白いこととやらを聞いてみようか。それとも他の話題を振ってみようか。こんなとき、おしゃべりの上手い森里君ならどうするんだろう。
lines.english: What now? Ask about the interesting thing? Try another subject? What would Morisato, master of easy conversation, do at a time like this?

lines.japanese: 「そっちは？　最近なんか面白いことあった？」
lines.english: “What about you? Anything interesting happen lately?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: もたもたしてたら、向こうから話題転換を持ちかけられた。そういえば渡来さんも、教室では森里君タイプに属するひとだった。
lines.english: While I was busy floundering, she supplied the change of subject herself. Come to think of it, Watarai belonged to Morisato’s conversational species when she was in the classroom.

lines.japanese: 「あ、面白いこと？　ええと、そうだな……」
lines.english: “Oh, something interesting? Let’s see, um…”

lines.japanese: 僕は慌てて記憶を探った。面白いこと。面白いこと。ルカ君の書き込みやそれに対する僕の感想は……きっと面白いの部類には入らないだろう。
lines.english: I scrambled through my memory. Something interesting. Something interesting. Ruka’s posts, and my thoughts about them… probably did not qualify.

lines.japanese: 急ぎブラウザの履歴を辿りながら考える。ある少年漫画をべつの作品風にコラージュしたパロディはすごく面白かったけど、元ネタを知らないであろう彼女にまでその感動が伝わるはずはない。
lines.english: I raced back through my browser history as I thought. There had been a hilarious parody that recast one boys’ manga in the style of another, but the joke could hardly move her as it had moved me when she almost certainly would not know the source material.

lines.japanese: 通りすがりのブログで拾った興味深いニュースならいくつかあるけど、一年生のとき森里君に「あのさ、外国のびっくり人間トピックスとかいちいち俺に報告しなくていいから」と言われて不評だった思い出がある。
lines.english: I had picked up a few intriguing news stories from blogs I wandered past, but in our first year Morisato had given those poor reviews: “Listen, you don’t have to report every single bizarre-people story from overseas to me.”

lines.japanese: アニメやゲームの話にいたっては「いや、コレ親切で言うんだけどさ、そういうの興味ない人種に語っちゃうのやめときな」と珍しく真剣な口調で諭されたことがあった。
lines.english: As for anime and games, he had once taken the rare step of warning me in perfect earnest: “I’m saying this for your own good, man. You’ve got to stop talking about that stuff to people who aren’t into it.”

lines.japanese: やむを得ず、僕はオフラインでの実体験をさかのぼった。
lines.english: With no other choice, I began combing backward through things that had happened to me offline.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ。おれ、さっき風呂場で居眠りして溺れかけた」
lines.english: “Oh, wait. I dozed off in the bath earlier and almost drowned.”

lines.japanese: 「わー、微笑ましー。ゲンブツくん的うっかりだね」
lines.english: “Aww, adorable. A blunder straight out of the funny pages.”

lines.japanese: 僕が必死にひねり出したユーモアは、朝刊に載ってるファミリー向け４コマと同レベルの評価だった。
lines.english: The humor I had wrung from myself in desperation earned the same reception as a family-friendly four-panel comic in the morning paper.

lines.japanese: いや……いや、違うんだ。
lines.english: No… no, that was not it.

lines.japanese: たしかに彼女は「面白いこと」って言ったけど、それはべつに笑い話に限定してるわけじゃないんだ。たぶん、会話のきっかけになるカンバセーションピースを要求しているだけなんだ。
lines.english: True, she had asked for something interesting, but that did not mean it had to be a funny story. She was probably just asking for a conversation piece—something, anything, that might get us talking.

lines.japanese: だから、何でもいい……何でもいいから、何か話題を……。
lines.english: So anything would do… Anything. I just needed some subject, some little thing to say…

lines.japanese: そして、あわよくば会話をどっか遊び行こうか的な方向へ……。
lines.english: And then, if fortune happened to favor me, I might somehow steer us toward maybe-we-should-go-somewhere-together territory…

lines.japanese: 無言の間が数秒続いた。ラジオだったら放送事故扱いになってしまう時間だ。
lines.english: The silence stretched for several seconds—long enough to count as dead air on the radio.

lines.japanese: 「うん。ありがと。ごめんね、テスト前の忙しいときに」
lines.english: “Okay. Thanks. And sorry to bother you when you’re so busy studying.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ううん、それは全然……」
lines.english: “Oh, no, that’s completely fine…”

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ」
lines.english: “Anyway, I should go.”

lines.japanese: そして受話口の小さな穴から、ついにその言葉が涌きでた。
lines.english: And at last those words welled from the tiny holes in the receiver.
“…Okay.”

lines.japanese: また明日、と彼女が言いのこして通話は切れた。
lines.english: “See you tomorrow,” she said, and the call ended.

lines.japanese: 僕は無機質な声で泣きつづける電話機をゆっくり耳から遠ざけ、ぼんやりと通話終了ボタンを押した。押したまましばらく動かなかった。
lines.english: Slowly, I drew the phone and its cold, unfeeling wail away from my ear. I pressed the button to end the call, then stayed there for a while, my finger still resting on it.

lines.japanese: サントラＣＤの演奏が終わっていたことに気付いた。
lines.english: Only then did I notice that the soundtrack CD had stopped playing.

lines.japanese: 小鳩の部屋も静かになっている。
lines.english: Kobato’s room had fallen silent too.

lines.japanese: 僕の部屋もまた静かだった。
lines.english: So had mine.

lines.japanese: 静かすぎる部屋で、僕はグレタガルドから帰ってきたときみたいに、しばらく呆然としていた。
lines.english: In that room, far too quiet now, I sat dazed for a while, just as I did whenever I returned from Gretagard.

lines.japanese: あの触れざる金色の粒子が、見えたような、見えないような。
lines.english: For a moment, I almost saw those untouchable golden particles. Or perhaps I did not.

lines.japanese: ……ああ。
lines.english: …Ah.

lines.japanese: ……ああ、そうだ。さっさと数学と世界史の予習を始めなくては。
lines.english: …Right. I needed to get started on tomorrow’s math and world-history material.

lines.japanese: 最後にキーボードのＦ５キーを押した。瑠樺君の新作に、まだレスポンスは付いてなかった。
lines.english: One last time, I pressed F5. Ruka’s new work still had no responses.

lines.japanese: 「よし……やるか……」
lines.english: “All right… Let’s do this…”

lines.japanese: 電話を充電器に戻し、パソコンの電源を落として、僕はのそのそと勉強机に移動した。
lines.english: I returned the phone to its charger, shut down the computer, and dragged myself over to my desk.

lines.japanese: まずは数学からだ。
lines.english: Math first.

lines.japanese: 数学は苦手な方なんだけど、でも掴みどころのない三角関数や二次方程式も、数ある現実の中ではまだ付きあいやすい方だと思う。
lines.english: Math was not my strong suit. Even so, elusive things like trigonometric functions and quadratic equations seemed among the easier of all these realities to get along with.
